effort: Carry controlled curved momentum into a clean exit while consolidating strength load.
brief: E2 combines a curved entry with one planned plant. Lateral skips supply rhythmic side force, a figure-eight changes curvature continuously, carioca rehearses alternating hip crossings, a two-vector bound changes landing direction, and an arcing shuffle exit avoids forcing every transition into a sharp corner.
marker: In E2, record whether the athlete controls lean on the arc, brakes before the declared plant and exits along the tangent-relative 90-degree line without a recovery hop.
readiness: Keep arc speed modest; this class is not a maximum-speed curved sprint test. Verify comfortable carioca foot placement and each bound landing before linking the two flights. Previous written doses are not evidence of recovery.
space: Use a measured 9 m × 6 m clear bay for arcs and the figure-eight, including each final 2.5 m stopping path. Mark radii rather than using random cone spacing. Only one route is active at a time; the three separate lanes do not confirm this shared width.

drills.name: Lateral Skip — two cycles
drills.execution: Step laterally then make a small hop on that leading leg, gather and repeat once; no maximal distance. Travel no more than 1 m per two-cycle attempt.
drills.job: Produce repeatable lateral push rhythm without a long approach or sharp plant.
drills.layout: Along the lane axis while facing across it; finish after two step-hop cycles and settle in place.
drills.difference: Step-hop skip rhythm with repeated same-leg support, unlike bilateral pogos or opposite-leg bounding.
drills.regress: Reduce step/hop size if rhythm needs crossed feet or trunk sway.
drills.exposure: 2 unilateral hop landings per direction, plus two ordinary entry steps; not sprint metres.

drills.name: Curved Run to Cut
drills.execution: Run a quarter arc of radius 1.25 m, brake before its end, plant into a 90-degree change relative to the incoming tangent, accelerate 1.5 m and stop over 2.5 m.
drills.job: Main curved-entry braking and force redirection, with the turn point declared in advance.
drills.layout: Arc length about 1.96 m; mark tangent and perpendicular exit so the cut angle is unambiguous. Clear a 2 m tangent abort corridor.
drills.difference: Curved entry is followed by a discrete planted cut; Class 7's curved run only decelerated to a terminal stop.
drills.regress: Lower arc speed if leaning persists through the plant or the athlete cannot find the exit line.
drills.exposure: 1 planted cut and 2 locomotor braking episodes.

drills.name: Figure-8 Cone Run
drills.execution: Run one smooth figure-eight around two cones, one full loop each, then leave on the marked tangent and stop over 2.5 m. Controlled speed, no cone touches.
drills.job: Change the direction of body lean smoothly between left and right curves.
drills.layout: Use two tangent circles of radius 0.75 m, centres 1.5 m apart; total curved travel about 9.42 m. The footprint is compact even though route travel exceeds lane length. Clear the crossing and final tangent stop.
drills.difference: Two opposing continuous loops with an inflection, not a single curved stop or a sharp cone cut.
drills.regress: Slow the loops if the athlete cuts across the circles or loses posture at the crossing.
drills.exposure: Continuous curving with 1 terminal stop; 0 discrete planted cuts counted.

drills.name: Carioca Quick Hips
drills.execution: Travel 2 m using alternating front and behind crossover contacts, then decelerate over 1.5 m. Keep the hips moving smoothly and the feet low.
drills.job: Reorganize hip crossing without stopping the lateral travel each step.
drills.layout: Move along the long axis of the lane, facing across it; start near 2, travel to 4 and stop by 5.5, then mirror.
drills.difference: Alternating front/behind crossing gait rather than crossover running with only an open forward crossing.
drills.regress: Reduce cadence and step width if feet tangle; retain a crisp push without chasing speed.
drills.exposure: 1 lateral-gait pass and terminal stop; no prescribed flight landings.

drills.name: Diagonal-to-Lateral Bound Pattern
drills.execution: Bound diagonally forward to the opposite leg, then redirect laterally onto the original leg; hold the second landing 2 s. Each flight stays within 0.4 m.
drills.job: Accept one vector and send the next push along a different vector without an extra setup hop.
drills.layout: Mark the two small landing targets in a 3 m × 3 m clear area. One continuous two-contact bounding pattern, not two separate sets.
drills.difference: The two flights change between diagonal and lateral vectors; the earlier skater pair reversed along one lateral line.
drills.regress: Shorten both flights if the first landing cannot support the second push.
drills.exposure: 2 unilateral landings, one each leg, per pattern.

drills.name: Shuffle Arc to Running Exit
drills.execution: Shuffle 1 m, smoothly open into a quarter arc of radius 1 m, then run 1.5 m along its tangent and stop over 2.5 m. No abrupt planted corner.
drills.job: Let the hips and force direction change progressively when a rounded exit is appropriate.
drills.layout: The declared path is 1 + 1.57 + 1.5 m, with a separate 2.5 m stop. Mark the arc so it stays inside the measured bay.
drills.difference: Continuous curving gait transition rather than Class 2's abrupt orthogonal shuffle-to-sprint corner.
drills.regress: Reduce entry speed if the arc becomes an uncontrolled pivot or cross-step stumble.
drills.exposure: 0 discrete planted cuts; 1 terminal braking episode.

light.job: Control pelvis orientation over one leg while the travel direction curves.
Maintain hip support against drifting toward the outside of the curve.

strength.job: Load hip force with single-leg pelvic control relevant to curved stance contacts.
Retain frontal acceptance strength for the curve-to-cut plant.
Retain lead-leg knee/hip force through the exit step.
Maintain heel-dig knee-flexor support for curved-entry braking.
Maintain adductor/pelvis support through changing lean.
Maintain bent-knee ankle force without increasing lower-leg rounds.

previous_review: Class 7 prescribed four discrete running cuts, four bilateral and two unilateral landings with six strength rounds. No actual tolerance is established.
progression: New curved and crossing patterns consolidate directional control at modest speed; only E2 contains a discrete running cut. Longer figure-eight path is paced as short skill practice with 120 s recovery, not conditioning.
strength_progression: Keep one working round in all six slots. Replace the bilateral hinge with one supported single-leg hinge round for pelvis control; load is newly calibrated and not compared directly with a bilateral RDL load. Other anchors hold their reduced doses.
audit: Defined curve radii and separated path length from floor footprint. Removed a pure curved-acceleration drill that would repeat the previous curved-run stop under another intent label. Capped each two-vector bound pattern at two flights.
next: Next class links discrete changes in short routes; review actual cumulative plants and landings before increasing route complexity.

light_entries.name: Hip Airplane — supported
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight, hand support and slight hip hinge. Slowly open/close pelvis through a small owned arc without rolling the stance foot.
light_entries.rest: Keep easy; rest 30 s between legs.
light_entries.regress: Reduce arc or use more hand support if knee/foot rotates uncontrollably.
light_entries.job: Control pelvis orientation over one leg while the travel direction curves.

light_entries.name: Mini-Band Lateral Walk
light_entries.execution: Very light loop above knees; small quiet steps, toes forward and knees aligned. Both directions are one set round.
light_entries.regress: Use a lighter band/smaller step if pelvis sways or the task burns.
light_entries.job: Maintain hip support against drifting toward the outside of the curve.

strength_entries.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift — supported dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: Light fingertip support; hold dumbbell in opposite hand, keep pelvis level and hinge 2 s down through controlled range.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce range/load when pelvis opens; support should remove balance as the load limiter.
strength_entries.job: Load hip force with single-leg pelvic control relevant to curved stance contacts.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Retain frontal acceptance strength for the curve-to-cut plant.

strength_entries.name: Split Squat — two dumbbells, both feet on floor
strength_entries.execution: **3 s down**, smooth forceful rise; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs, 120 s between rounds**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep full front-foot pressure and knee travel aligned with the foot. Reduce load/range for heel lift, knee drift or trunk collapse.
strength_entries.job: Retain lead-leg knee/hip force through the exit step.

strength_entries.name: Glute Bridge Iso Hold — long-lever hamstring variant
strength_entries.execution: bilateral. Heels farther from the hips than a standard bridge, knees still bent; bodyweight or a securely hand-held sandbag over the pelvis to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Try to pull the heels toward the body without sliding them; keep ribs down. Bring heels closer or remove load for cramp/lost height; stop for symptoms.
strength_entries.job: Maintain heel-dig knee-flexor support for curved-entry braking.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Maintain adductor/pelvis support through changing lean.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Maintain bent-knee ankle force without increasing lower-leg rounds.
